findings.claim: you judge it by time and touch, not by looking
findings.because: A salt crust cannot be judged by touch. The dish is judged by time for its weight, or by a probe thermometer pushed through the crust into the thickest part (or in at the gill opening); every standard method uses one of these.
findings.fix: you judge it by time for its weight, or by a probe pushed through the crust, not by looking

findings.fix: then the stack roasts in a hot oven and the slices are seared hard on the plancha as you carve

findings.claim: Cook the pastor first: it tells you whether your fire holds a zone before you commit a whole brisket to it.
findings.because: The home trompo is oven-roasted (brief technique: "Roasting in a hot oven"; no live-fire technique is listed for it), so it tests no fire and no two-zone setup. findings.fix: Cook the pastor first: it roasts in the oven and finishes on the plancha, a plate you can put up in one day before the brisket takes twelve hours.

findings.claim: Low and slow smoking is the whole dish
findings.because: The brief's item lists three techniques for Central Texas Smoked Brisket: Braising, Low & slow smoking, and Resting meat & slicing against the grain. The wrapped stretch through the stall is a braise in the meat's own juices, so smoking is not the whole dish.

findings.claim: The nine atlas entries turn up for a fortnight a year, each with one handling rule.

Cardoon and Puntarelle are winter vegetables carried for months (Puntarelle's brief text is a Roman winter salad; Cardoon's field blanching runs "for weeks" ahead of a long season), Lion's Mane is cultivated year round (the brief distinguishes cultivated mycelium from fruiting body), Mangosteen and Tamarillo are imported across long seasons, and White Truffle runs roughly October to December. Only Matsutake and Medlar are anything like a fortnight, and even they run weeks. The brief gives no season length for any of them.

findings.fix: Cardoon is field-blanched against its bitterness and most of it is boiled in acidulated water first
